import pandas as pd

# Load source tables
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_78/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_78/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_78/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source0 and Source1 on user_id to get sex for each rating
df = source0.merge(source1[['user_id', 'sex']], on='user_id', how='left')

# Join the above result with Source2 on movie_id to get movie titles
df = df.merge(source2[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='left')

# Group by movie_id and title, aggregate average rating filtered by sex
result = df.groupby(['movie_id', 'title']).agg(
    F = ('rating', lambda x: x[df.loc[x.index, 'sex'] == 'F'].mean()),
    M = ('rating', lambda x: x[df.loc[x.index, 'sex'] == 'M'].mean())
).reset_index()

# Ensure correct dtypes
result['movie_id'] = result['movie_id'].astype(int)
result['title'] = result['title'].astype(str)
result['F'] = result['F'].astype(float)
result['M'] = result['M'].astype(float)

# Save to target path
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_78/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_78/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_78/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_78/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_78_0 and Source3_78_1 on user_id
join_0_1 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_78_2 on movie_id
joined = pd.merge(join_0_1, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Filter ratings by sex and compute average ratings per movie_id and title
# Group by movie_id and title (leftmost non-float unique columns in target)
grouped = joined.groupby(["movie_id", "title"], as_index=False).agg(
    F = ("rating", lambda x: x[joined.loc[x.index, "sex"] == 'F'].mean()),
    M = ("rating", lambda x: x[joined.loc[x.index, "sex"] == 'M'].mean())
)

# Write output with exact target schema and column names
grouped.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_78/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
